organizations.name: UN Monitoring Team
aliases: UN Security Council Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team
organizations.notes: 10 experts with intelligence/financial/legal/diplomatic backgrounds; reports (~10,500 words) built from member-state intelligence, triangulated; Taliban trashes every report; report drafted December 2023

organizations.name: al-Qaeda
organizations.notes: Led de facto by Saif al-Adel from Iran; training camps in 10 of 34 Afghan provinces, madrasas in 5, weapons depot in Panjshir, safe houses in Herat/Farah/Helmand/Kabul, facilitation network to Iran; decentralized media but centralized media strategy; exploited 7 October

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Denies Zawahiri was in Kabul; trashes every UN report; concerned about embarrassment from extremists; colluding with TTP against Pakistan; in talks with Iran on managing al-Qaeda risk

organizations.name: AQAP
organizations.notes: Al-Qaeda tightened control via Saif al-Adel's son Khalid; possible truce with Houthis; attacks mainly on Saudi/UAE/Yemeni government; media and external-ops (IED) specialization; ramped up propaganda after 7 Oct

organizations.name: Houthis
organizations.notes: UN report: AQAP may be in a truce with the Houthis

organizations.name: AQIS
organizations.notes: UN: licensed involvement with TTP in terrorist activity against Pakistan

organizations.name: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan
aliases: Movement of the Taliban in Pakistan
organizations.notes: Supported by al-Qaeda; suicide bombers trained in al-Qaeda camps in Afghanistan; launching far more attacks in Pakistan than ISIS does anywhere

organizations.name: Islamic State Khorasan Province
organizations.notes: UN assesses ISKP the greater external threat (Roggio disagrees); attack in Iran; uses Central Asians (Tajiks, Uzbeks) for European plots; own Tajik/Uzbek-language propaganda; received ~$25,000/month from al-Karrar office; UN retracted earlier claim about its leader

organizations.name: Islamic State
organizations.notes: Succession of caliphs with shortening life expectancy; new caliph Abu Hafs unknown; UN hints leadership may be shifting away from Iraq/Syria and toward geographically dispersed model; centralized media

organizations.name: General Directorate of Provinces
organizations.notes: Oversees ISIS regional offices; headed by Abu Sara al-Iraqi until his death; 'more relevant than the actual caliph'

organizations.name: al-Karrar office
organizations.notes: ISIS regional office led by Bilal al-Sudani; essential funding node; moved money to Mozambique, DRC, South Africa and Afghanistan; funded by crime (extortion, taxes, kidnapping) pooled in Somalia and South Africa

organizations.name: al-Furqan office
organizations.notes: ISIS regional office hosted by ISWAP; one of three offices; may be taking on al-Karrar's role

organizations.name: ISWAP

organizations.name: Boko Haram

organizations.name: Ansaru
organizations.notes: Al-Qaeda's nominal Nigerian branch; bogged down fighting bandits; below expected capability

organizations.name: JNIM

organizations.name: ISGS
aliases: Islamic State in the Greater Sahara

events.description: Release of the latest UN Monitoring Team report on al-Qaeda/ISIL (drafted December 2023), discussed in this episode
Zawahiri killed in a US strike in Kabul; Saif al-Adel took over without public announcement; Taliban deny he was there
Hamas 7 October attack; al-Qaeda, especially AQAP from Yemen, ramped up propaganda to exploit the Gaza war
Khalid Saif al-Adel's travels to southern Yemen intensified from mid-August, protected by Ibrahim al-Banna
actors: Khalid Saif al-Adel (Muhammad Salah al-Din Zaidan)

events.description: Nasir al-Wuhayshi killed in US drone strike (host's date; actual 2015)
1998 US embassy bombings; al-Qaeda bombers trained in Lebanon by Hezbollah on Iran's orders
Al-Shabaab and JNIM 'Jerusalem will not be Judaized' propaganda campaigns, indicating central al-Qaeda direction

Al-Qaeda opened eight new training camps in four additional Afghan provinces (now 10 of 34), runs madrasas in five provinces, a weapons depot in Panjshir, safe houses in Herat, Farah, Helmand and Kabul, and a facilitation network into Iran across three provinces
ISIL-Khorasan attack in Iran, 'a big one'
Abu Sara al-Iraqi, head of the ISIS General Directorate of Provinces, killed (reported in previous UN report, 'a year ago')
Abu Hafs al-Hashimi al-Qurashi named new ISIS caliph; identity, nationality and location unknown
Bilal al-Sudani, head of ISIS al-Karrar office, killed by US forces over funding of ISIL operations in Afghanistan
Previous UN report: al-Karrar office sending about $25,000 a month to ISKP
Al-Qaeda took over northern Mali with the help of Tuareg groups
JNIM–ISGS truce/detente since summer 2023, confirmed by UN: JNIM cedes Menaka to ISGS, ISGS refrains from attacking JNIM in the tri-border area
Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger break away from ECOWAS; MINUSMA evacuating Mali; France lost influence
Ibn Omar, former leader of IS Mozambique, killed ('last year')
IS Mozambique reoccupied villages and a town in Macomia district, first large territorial occupation since 2021, as SADC forces prepare to withdraw
Two al-Shabaab members, including the son of a senior leader, arrested in Costa Rica in the last couple of months
Al-Shabaab member arrested in the Philippines taking flight lessons; another arrested months later in an East African country

key_claims: Saif al-Adel runs al-Qaeda from Iran but cannot be announced because the Taliban deny Zawahiri was ever killed in Kabul.

Al-Qaeda is building infrastructure in Taliban-ruled Afghanistan: camps in 10 provinces, madrasas, a Panjshir weapons depot, safe houses near the Iranian border and a facilitation network into Iran; Roggio argues this makes AQ a greater threat than ISKP, contrary to the UN's assessment.
The Afghan Taliban and AQIS are colluding with the TTP in attacks on Pakistan, with TTP suicide bombers trained in al-Qaeda camps.
Saif al-Adel's son Khalid is al-Qaeda's instrument for tightening control over AQAP from Yemen; AQAP may have a truce with the Houthis.
Al-Qaeda's decentralized media with a centralized strategy let it exploit 7 October faster than ISIS.
ISIS may be shifting from short-lived Iraqi caliphs in Syria to a geographically dispersed leadership model; the real power sat with GDP head Abu Sara al-Iraqi and al-Karrar's Bilal al-Sudani.
The JNIM–ISGS truce and JNIM's alliances with Tuareg factions have created a contiguous jihadist battlespace from Mauritania to Cameroon.
Al-Shabaab remains resilient with 7-12k fighters and ~$100M/yr and is going global (pilot training, Costa Rica arrests); the humanitarian carve-out and Somalia-committee sanctions are criticized.
The 'no direct command and control' caveat for IS Mozambique/ISCAP is a member-state talking point the hosts reject.
